Every place north of the Arctic Circle h.why: The textbook fact about the polar circles: Wikipedia's first sentence on the midnight sun puts it in the summer months north of the Arctic Circle, and the Arctic Circle article defines the line by the summer and winter solstices. The phrase is common in Dolma, while the new value is almost never written.

sources.quote: Midnight sun, also known as polar day, is a natural phenomenon that occurs in the summer months in places north of the Arctic Circle or south of the Antarctic Circle, when the Sun remains visible at the local midnight.
The Arctic Circle marks the southernmost latitude for which at the December solstice (winter) the Sun does not rise and at the June solstice (summer) the Sun does not set.

sources.note: The new value, rare (13 against 1,614 for summer).

notes: TBox revision, rewritten 2026-11-11. The earlier edit (every fjord is an unglaciated river valley) shared its subject with the reviewed example geography-replace-0903 (fjords), which the main split may not do (CRITERIA Rule 4), so the record now edits another well-known class rule: places north of the Arctic Circle have their midnight sun in summer, moved to winter. Derivability very_unlikely: the rule is stated directly (Wikipedia's first sentence on the midnight sun). No real exceptions: north of the circle the sun stays up around the June solstice; refraction only widens the zone slightly south of the line. Relation has_midnight_sun_in (staging, functional). The three derived queries name a real but little-known town north of the circle and ask the season (inheritance, 2 hops: the edited rule plus the membership the prompt states); none of the three has its midnight sun written down in Dolma (exact phrases 0, a handful of co-occurrences). Famous midnight-sun places (Tromsø, Kiruna, the North Cape, Utqiagvik) are not asked, since a model may hold their season by name. The third is an application: a trip plan whose answer is the season, without naming the options. Residual risk, recorded rather than removed: a model can reach 'summer' from astronomy (the June solstice) instead of the class rule, a background route every polar place shares. Near unrelated: the season of the longest days at a place south of the circle; an edit that flips seasons in general would answer winter there, and its reference differs from the new answer. Every bridge is stated in its prompt, so only the propositional side facts need checks. The paired contraction record (geography-delete-0005) still removes the old fjord rule and needs re-pairing to this edit.
